Chosen opening: measuring which atoms directly transmit restoring forces

I’m choosing local identification of restoring-force couplings in an assembled material as the next principal direction. The useful operation is to distinguish a direct mechanical interaction from correlated motion produced by the surrounding structure. That distinction matters when deciding whether to change a chemical bond, alter its environment, or revise the material model used to predict an intervention.

There is now a substantive theoretical result, a discriminating construction, and an initial physical test. The proposed observable contains the desired information. Two ordinary overlapping electron probes do not yet isolate it. The unresolved interface is consequently quite specific.

The earlier mass witness, returned mediator, static-label comparison and withdrawn small-motif justification retain their previous scope. None of the calculations below upgrades isotope identification, survival, transfer chemistry or beamtime estimates.

1. The information that is missing

Recent experiments provide a particularly relevant starting point. Atomic-scale electron interferometry has measured directional vibrational correlations between adjacent silicon columns. Its interpretation uses an effective harmonic-chain model that incorporates the surrounding crystal through an on-site restraint. That is a substantial realised capability and the closest comparator for this opening. It does not make the conversion from a local correlation to a direct interaction independent of the environmental model. Nature

For a classical harmonic material, the distinction is explicit. Divide its coordinates into the observed region RRR and an unobserved environment EEE. The observed equilibrium covariance determines

kBT CR−1=KRR−KREKEE−1KER.k_BT\,C_R^{-1} = K_{RR}-K_{RE}K_{EE}^{-1}K_{ER}.kB​TCR−1​=KRR​−KRE​KEE−1​KER​.

Here KKK is the force-constant matrix. The right-hand side includes relaxation of the environment. A direct measurement of KRRK_{RR}KRR​ would answer a different question: what restoring force changes immediately when a selected coordinate moves, with the other nuclear coordinates held fixed?

This is ordinary static condensation, not a new mechanical theorem. Its consequence for the proposed operation is important: a change in measured local compliance need not mean that the local interaction itself changed.

The opportunity is to obtain a local dynamical quantity that separates those contributions without first fitting the whole surrounding network.

2. An exact cross-spectrum identity supplies the target observable

Take a nuclear Hamiltonian

H=∑ipi22mi+V(R),H=\sum_i\frac{\mathbf p_i^2}{2m_i}+V(\mathbf R),H=i∑​2mi​pi2​​+V(R),

with a scalar, position-dependent potential and a time-reversal-invariant equilibrium state. Let Ai(Ri)A_i(\mathbf R_i)Ai​(Ri​) and Bj(Rj)B_j(\mathbf R_j)Bj​(Rj​) be scattering operators acting on different atoms, i≠ji\neq ji=j.

Define their cross spectrum by

SAB(E)=∑n,mpnAmn∗Bmn δ ⁣(E−Em+En),S_{AB}(E)= \sum_{n,m}p_n A_{mn}^{*}B_{mn} \,\delta\!\left(E-E_m+E_n\right),SAB​(E)=n,m∑​pn​Amn∗​Bmn​δ(E−Em​+En​),

and its real signed moments by

Cr(A,B)=Re⁡∫−∞∞ErSAB(E) dE.C_r(A,B)=\operatorname{Re}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} E^r S_{AB}(E)\,dE.Cr​(A,B)=Re∫−∞∞​ErSAB​(E)dE.

“Signed” means that energy gain and energy loss both enter, with their actual signs. A cross spectrum is an interference quantity; it need not be positive.

The identities I derived are

C1(Ai,Bj)=0\boxed{C_1(A_i,B_j)=0}C1​(Ai​,Bj​)=0​

and

C3(Ai,Bj)=ℏ42mimjRe⁡⟨∇iAi∗⋅∂2V∂Ri∂Rj⋅∇jBj⟩.\boxed{ C_3(A_i,B_j) = \frac{\hbar^4}{2m_i m_j} \operatorname{Re} \left\langle \nabla_i A_i^{*}\cdot \frac{\partial^2V}{\partial\mathbf R_i\partial\mathbf R_j} \cdot\nabla_j B_j \right\rangle . }C3​(Ai​,Bj​)=2mi​mj​ℏ4​Re⟨∇i​Ai∗​⋅∂Ri​∂Rj​∂2V​⋅∇j​Bj​⟩.​

This does not require a harmonic potential, Gaussian displacements or a one-phonon approximation. It does require the stated Hamiltonian and separate atomic support of the two operators.

The essential algebra is short. Writing LB=[H,B]\mathcal L B=[H,B]LB=[H,B], the relevant odd moment is obtained from the nested commutator. For distinct atoms,

[Ai†,LBj]=0,[A_i^\dagger,\mathcal L B_j]=0,[Ai†​,LBj​]=0,

whereas

[Ai†,L3Bj]=ℏ4mimj∇iAi∗⋅Vij′′⋅∇jBj.[A_i^\dagger,\mathcal L^3 B_j] = \frac{\hbar^4}{m_i m_j} \nabla_i A_i^*\cdot V_{ij}''\cdot\nabla_j B_j.[Ai†​,L3Bj​]=mi​mj​ℏ4​∇i​Ai∗​⋅Vij′′​⋅∇j​Bj​.

The local kinetic and recoil contributions disappear from this cross term. The mixed force derivative remains.

For linear displacement probes, this becomes especially transparent:

C3(uiα,ujβ)=ℏ42mimj⟨Kiα,jβ⟩.C_3(u_{i\alpha},u_{j\beta}) = \frac{\hbar^4}{2m_i m_j} \left\langle K_{i\alpha,j\beta}\right\rangle .C3​(uiα​,ujβ​)=2mi​mj​ℏ4​⟨Kiα,jβ​⟩.

For nonlinear scattering probes, it measures a probe-weighted mixed curvature, rather than an unweighted bond constant. A zero weighted result can also arise from cancellation, so a null signal alone is not a universal certificate of no interaction.

I checked the nonlinear identity against explicit quantum spectra of two coupled anharmonic oscillators, including individual quartic terms and a quartic coupling. Increasing the oscillator basis from 12 to 18 to 24 states per coordinate brought the largest discrepancy in the tested cases down to approximately 2.1×10−62.1\times10^{-6}2.1×10−6 relative error. The first cross moment remained at numerical zero. This is a check of the derivation, not a material calibration.

A useful connection to the retained mass witness

For a centred symmetric energy-resolution kernel with variance σE2\sigma_E^2σE2​,

C~3=C3+3σE2C1.\widetilde C_3=C_3+3\sigma_E^2 C_1.C3​=C3​+3σE2​C1​.

Thus the ideal distinct-atom cross moment is unchanged by symmetric instrumental broadening because C1=0C_1=0C1​=0. Individual phonon peaks need not be resolved to define this quantity.

That protection concerns the mean full-spectrum moment. It does not remove shot noise, energy-origin drift, spectral truncation or electronic backgrounds. When real probes overlap, C1C_1C1​ is generally nonzero; measuring it supplies the corresponding broadening correction and a diagnostic of lost selectivity.

The underlying connection between spectral moments and force constants is established science. Nuclear-resonant inelastic X-ray spectroscopy already extracts mean force constants from third moments, with treatments extending beyond harmonic potentials. The proposed addition here is a local cross-channel operation aimed at distinguishing direct coupling from environmental mediation, not a claim to have invented force-sensitive sum rules. ScienceDirect+1

3. A stronger discriminating construction

A simple two-site example would be too weak a comparison: additional temperature measurements or individual-site spectra might distinguish it. I therefore constructed a stronger pair of stable quantum harmonic models.

They have:

  • Identical individual-site vibrational spectra at every energy.
  • Identical joint displacement distributions of the two observed coordinates at 300, 500 and 900 K.
  • Different direct force coupling between those coordinates.

This is an identifiability construction, not a proposed chemical composition.

Construction and physical consistency

Use six mode energies,

Eν=(20,  40,  65,  100,  150,  220) meV,E_\nu=(20,\;40,\;65,\;100,\;150,\;220)\ {\rm meV},Eν​=(20,40,65,100,150,220) meV,

each with twofold degeneracy. The spectral weight of each doublet on the two observed coordinates is

Wν=(1/6cνcν1/6).W_\nu= \begin{pmatrix} 1/6&c_\nu\\ c_\nu&1/6 \end{pmatrix}.Wν​=(1/6cν​​cν​1/6​).

at each of the three temperatures, while

∑νcνAEν2=0,∑νcνBEν2≠0.\sum_\nu c_\nu^{A}E_\nu^2=0, \qquad \sum_\nu c_\nu^{B}E_\nu^2\ne0.ν∑​cνA​Eν2​=0,ν∑​cνB​Eν2​=0.

These are compatible spectral weights of a common Hamiltonian. Every WνW_\nuWν​ is positive definite—the smallest eigenvalue across both constructions exceeds 0.10050.10050.1005—and ∑νWν=I2\sum_\nu W_\nu=I_2∑ν​Wν​=I2​. Concatenating their square roots gives two orthonormal rows, which can be completed to an orthogonal normal-mode matrix. Assigning the specified positive mode energies then constructs a stable 12-coordinate harmonic Hamiltonian.

With coordinate masses of 121212 atomic mass units, the resulting direct coupling is

Because the states are Gaussian, matching these matrices matches the entire two-coordinate displacement distribution at those temperatures. The unchanged diagonal spectral weights also make all individual-site vibrational spectra identical.

The cross cubic moment distinguishes the models. For displacement probes it is zero in Model A and proportional to the stated nonzero coupling in Model B.

This establishes a useful information gap: individual-site spectroscopy plus a finite set of local equilibrium correlation measurements can leave direct force transmission undetermined. A measurement of the dynamical cross response can supply the missing information.

It is not an impossibility claim about other measurements. Observing more of the environment, using additional structural assumptions, or acquiring sufficiently informative coherent momentum-resolved data can also distinguish these models.

4. A specified electron-optical operation—and where it currently fails

There are relevant realised components. Inelastic electron Mach–Zehnder interferometry has demonstrated phase-sensitive interference after plasmon excitation. Electron holographic masks and programmable phase plates have demonstrated controlled wavefront shaping. These establish physical ways to prepare and interfere electron paths; they do not establish the proposed atomic force measurement as an assembly. arxiv.org+2

I specified the following passive-mask construction.

Starting with a finite circular pupil a0(κ)a_0(\boldsymbol\kappa)a0​(κ), use

a±(κ)=a0(κ)1±e−iκ⋅d2.a_\pm(\boldsymbol\kappa)= a_0(\boldsymbol\kappa) \frac{1\pm e^{-i\boldsymbol\kappa\cdot\mathbf d}}{2}.a±​(κ)=a0​(κ)21±e−iκ⋅d​.

These masks create coherent sums and differences of two shifted probes. Their transmission amplitude never exceeds one. With spectra normalised to the incident flux before the masks, their difference extracts the real cross spectrum. Additional relative phases supply the other quadrature.

This construction pays for unequal transmission. For the specified 60-keV, 32-mrad pupil and a 1.421.421.42-Å separation, the ideal mask transmissions are approximately 44.9% and 55.1%. Those are optical-model values, not measured fabrication efficiencies.

Common physical calculation

The initial calculation combined:

  • The retained screened neutral-carbon electron-scattering model.
  • A finite coherent incident pupil.
  • The published Perebeinos–Tersoff carbon valence-force model.
  • A 391-atom moving region with a clamped outer boundary.
  • Thermal displacement and velocity covariances generated by that same force matrix at 300 K.
  • Harmonic multiphonon contributions to the moments, rather than assigning independent phonon weights. The published force model supplies a physically grounded carbon test case, with its existing scope and limitations. arxiv.org

The important result is an obstruction: coherent shifted probes are not operators confined to separate atoms. Each probe couples to both target atoms and to additional neighbours.

For general probes A=∑iAiA=\sum_iA_iA=∑i​Ai​ and B=∑jBjB=\sum_jB_jB=∑j​Bj​,

C3(A,B)=∑i≠jC3(Ai,Bj)+∑iC3(Ai,Bi).C_3(A,B) = \sum_{i\ne j} C_3(A_i,B_j) + \sum_i C_3(A_i,B_i).C3​(A,B)=i=j∑​C3​(Ai​,Bj​)+i∑​C3​(Ai​,Bi​).

The second sum survives. It includes same-atom force, kinetic and recoil contributions.

At one specified outgoing direction, 110 mrad along the target bond, the first quadrature calculation gave the following decomposition:

Contribution to the cubic cross momentApproximate value, eV³ per incident electron per steradian
Same-atom terms−5.7×10−6-5.7\times10^{-6}−5.7×10−6
Intended atomic pair−9.8×10−7-9.8\times10^{-7}−9.8×10−7
Other distinct-atom pairs+2.6×10−7+2.6\times10^{-7}+2.6×10−7

The unwanted same-atom contribution was roughly six times the intended pair contribution. These are preliminary numerical diagnostics, not converged instrument predictions. The numerical runtime became unavailable before I could complete the convergence and probe-design calculations.

The physical lesson is firmer than those particular numbers: orthogonal or phase-controlled electron beams do not automatically provide independently localised atomic interaction channels. The first cross moment is useful for detecting overlap, but cancelling that one scalar does not prove that the cubic moment contains only the desired pair.

There is also a calibration trap to avoid. In this calculation the published force field supplies test truth. In an experiment, subtracting its predicted same-atom signal and then claiming to have independently measured that force field would be circular.

5. What the operation could add to the strongest alternatives

The opportunity is narrower than “measuring stiffness,” which is already well established.

Atomic correlation interferometry already provides local directional correlation information. The proposed cross moment would target a mixed force derivative with a different dependence on the environment. The counterexample shows why those are distinct observables; it does not invalidate the silicon experiment’s effective-chain interpretation.

Covariance-based reconstruction is independently effective when enough coordinates are observed and its statistical-mechanical assumptions hold. Video microscopy and covariance analysis have experimentally recovered vibrational information in colloidal crystals, including modes associated with structural defects. This would often be the better method at an optically accessible scale. arxiv.org

Nuclear-resonant spectroscopy already measures force-related moments and provides a strong benchmark for any claim of model-independent stiffness information. The possible addition here is spatial selection of a cross coupling, rather than a mean restraint on a resonant nucleus.

Conventional vibrational spectra and force-field fitting can remain preferable when the modes, structure and parameterisation are sufficiently constrained. The construction above demonstrates missing information in particular local inputs; it does not establish a universal efficiency advantage for cubic-moment acquisition.

The scientific payoff, if the physical separation can be obtained, is the ability to ask:

Did this local change alter the restoring interaction itself, or did it alter the surrounding structure through which the observed motion is coordinated?

That is useful for testing material models at defects and interfaces, and for predicting the immediate mechanical consequence of a local intervention. A mixed force constant still does not by itself determine an activated reaction barrier, failure rate or thermal conductivity.

6. The organising principle worth retaining

In a harmonic model, the odd cross moments form a hierarchy. With mass matrix MMM and dynamical matrix D=M−1/2KM−1/2D=M^{-1/2}KM^{-1/2}D=M−1/2KM−1/2,

C2n+1(ui,uj)=ℏ2n+22[M−1/2DnM−1/2]ij.C_{2n+1}(u_i,u_j) = \frac{\hbar^{2n+2}}{2} \left[M^{-1/2}D^nM^{-1/2}\right]_{ij}.C2n+1​(ui​,uj​)=2ℏ2n+2​[M−1/2DnM−1/2]ij​.

The cubic moment contains the direct force coupling. The fifth contains products of couplings, including paths through intermediate coordinates. This connects spectral cross information to the early-time propagation of a mechanical disturbance. It also explains why matching local fluctuations or individual-site spectra need not match the way an intervention propagates.

For anharmonic systems, the exact cubic identity survives in its weighted form. The simple higher-moment path interpretation requires the additional harmonic assumptions.

This is the principal branch I would sustain at the present boundary: obtaining local interaction information that ordinary local observations can leave hidden. The completed work gives it an independent scientific purpose and an exact target observable. The first physical construction exposes, rather than resolves, the decisive interface.

The next constructive question is whether a finite set of realisable probe masks can separate the desired mixed curvature from same-atom and neighbouring-pair contributions using independently acquired wavefront and material information. That question can change the case for the operation. Further isotope-reader calibration or beamtime estimates cannot answer it.

The physical lesson is firmer than those particular numbers: orthogonal or phase-controlled electron beams do not automatically provide independently localised atomic interaction channels. The first cross moment is useful for detecting overlap, but cancelling that one scalar does not prove that the cubic moment contains only the desired pair.

There is also a calibration trap to avoid. In this calculation the published force field supplies test truth. In an experiment, subtracting its predicted same-atom signal and then claiming to have independently measured that force field would be circular.

5. What the operation could add to the strongest alternatives

The opportunity is narrower than “measuring stiffness,” which is already well established.

Atomic correlation interferometry already provides local directional correlation information. The proposed cross moment would target a mixed force derivative with a different dependence on the environment. The counterexample shows why those are distinct observables; it does not invalidate the silicon experiment’s effective-chain interpretation.

Covariance-based reconstruction is independently effective when enough coordinates are observed and its statistical-mechanical assumptions hold. Video microscopy and covariance analysis have experimentally recovered vibrational information in colloidal crystals, including modes associated with structural defects. This would often be the better method at an optically accessible scale. 
arxiv.org

Nuclear-resonant spectroscopy already measures force-related moments and provides a strong benchmark for any claim of model-independent stiffness information. The possible addition here is spatial selection of a cross coupling, rather than a mean restraint on a resonant nucleus.

Conventional vibrational spectra and force-field fitting can remain preferable when the modes, structure and parameterisation are sufficiently constrained. The construction above demonstrates missing information in particular local inputs; it does not establish a universal efficiency advantage for cubic-moment acquisition.

The scientific payoff, if the physical separation can be obtained, is the ability to ask:

Did this local change alter the restoring interaction itself, or did it alter the surrounding structure through which the observed motion is coordinated?

That is useful for testing material models at defects and interfaces, and for predicting the immediate mechanical consequence of a local intervention. A mixed force constant still does not by itself determine an activated reaction barrier, failure rate or thermal conductivity.

The cubic moment contains the direct force coupling. The fifth contains products of couplings, including paths through intermediate coordinates. This connects spectral cross information to the early-time propagation of a mechanical disturbance. It also explains why matching local fluctuations or individual-site spectra need not match the way an intervention propagates.

For anharmonic systems, the exact cubic identity survives in its weighted form. The simple higher-moment path interpretation requires the additional harmonic assumptions.

This is the principal branch I would sustain at the present boundary: obtaining local interaction information that ordinary local observations can leave hidden. The completed work gives it an independent scientific purpose and an exact target observable. The first physical construction exposes, rather than resolves, the decisive interface.

The next constructive question is whether a finite set of realisable probe masks can separate the desired mixed curvature from same-atom and neighbouring-pair contributions using independently acquired wavefront and material information. That question can change the case for the operation. Further isotope-reader calibration or beamtime estimates cannot answer it.
